details:
Compared to hiding the entire room of avatars such that they all appear as robots, using the distance hiding feature seems to still cause lag, as if the avatars were still all loaded. On my GTX 1080, I would max out at around 59-60% VRAM usage while standing in a room full of 30+ hidden avatars while having all avatars shown but only the nearest *three* avatars shown made my VRAM sit at an unhealthy 92-100%, tanking my frames and often crashing when maxing out. It seems as if the way the game is hiding the avatars at a distance still has them loaded, at least partially in a way that causes performance drops.

Repro: Go into a crowded lobby with your safety settings forcing all avatars to be hidden and take a benchmark. Then, set your proximity avatar settings to something low and take another benchmark. The latter should perform noticeably worse.

Expected: The avatars hidden by proximity should not have any performance overhead, as their replaced model is even less detailed than the default robot avatar.

Actual: The game somehow runs even worse than if all models are loaded at once using the default robot model.
title: Proximity hidden avatars appear to cause performance issues
